leagues.name: Saudi-backed professional boxing (Riyadh Season, The Ring, Zuffa Boxing)
notes: Event-host shape: the entities are fight cards, not clubs, so no clubs are recorded; events are listed in unsourced. Saudi money appears in three forms: Riyadh Season (GEA) host/title deals on cards in Riyadh and abroad, Sela's 60% ownership of Zuffa Boxing (TKO holds 40%), and Turki Alalshikh's personal ownership of The Ring magazine and its belt brand.

Zuffa Boxing is a joint venture announced 5 Mar 2025 by Turki Alalshikh, TKO Group Holdings and Sela ('A Public Investment Fund (PIF) company', per the TKO release), TKO serving as managing partner. Thomas Hauser in The Guardian (28 Jan 2026) reports Sela owns 60% and TKO 40%; the split rests on that single press report and should be checked against TKO filings.

Paramount+ is the exclusive US/Canada/Latin America home of Zuffa Boxing from January 2026 (announced 29 Sep 2025); The Guardian reports Paramount is 'believed to be paying Zuffa Boxing $100m a year' for 12 cards.

The Ring magazine (The Ring Magazine FZ-LLC, Dubai) has been owned by Turki Alalshikh since November 2024; he is chairman of the General Entertainment Authority and president of the Saudi Boxing Federation. The Ring site's own partner wall lists PIF as its 'Strategic' partner and Saudi brands (anb, Visit Saudi, Saudia, stc, SRMG, HUMAIN, Sela, AROYA) among its tiered partners.

Zuffa Boxing and its allies lobbied for the Muhammad Ali American Boxing Revival Act (House-passed 24 Mar 2026, Senate pending), which would let 'Unified Boxing Organizations' combine promotion, rankings and titles - the Guardian (Hauser, 28 Jan 2026; Zidan, 1 Aug 2025) frames this as clearing the path for a Saudi-backed takeover of boxing governance.

Event lists on Wikipedia (Zuffa Boxing, The Ring, Riyadh Season) are mostly uncited; cards were cross-checked against Ring magazine, UFC.com, ESPN and press where possible. Zuffa events after June 2026 and further Riyadh Season 2026-27 cards were not fully captured.

owners.name: Turki Alalshikh (private individual)
owners.note: Bought 100% of The Ring Magazine in November 2024 in a personal deal (his own X post, 11 Nov 2024). Co-founded by Dana White and Turki Alalshikh.

claims.text: Zuffa Boxing and its allies lobbied for the Muhammad Ali Boxing Revival Act, which would let a 'Unified Boxing Organization' combine promotion, rankings and titles - removing Ali Act protections that separate promoters from sanctioning bodies. Thomas Hauser reports Zuffa's fighter contracts are less generous than the purses Turki Alalshikh had paid, and the Guardian's Karim Zidan writes the bill 'paves the way for Saudi to bypass established sanctioning bodies, undermine existing promoters, and ultimately, gut professional boxing'.
claims.short: Zuffa Boxing backed a US bill that would let it act as promoter, ranking body and title owner at once, weakening Ali Act fighter protections.

source.name: The Guardian - Thomas Hauser, 'Zuffa Boxing says it will save the sport - but the fine print shows that fighters may pay the price' (28 Jan 2026); Karim Zidan, 'How the Ali Act overhaul is clearing the path for a Saudi-backed takeover of boxing' (1 Aug 2025)
source.note: Second article: https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2025/aug/01/ali-act-saudi-boxing-reform-tko-zuffa-congress. The House passed the bill by voice vote on 24 Mar 2026 (ESPN, Michael Rothstein); Senate pending.

proposedRatings.reasoning: Riyadh Season is the entertainment arm of the Saudi state (GEA) and now puts its name on boxing cards in Riyadh, Las Vegas, London and New York. Same state tier as Visit Saudi and Riyadh Air: government-of-saudi-arabia record (record 345 executions in 2024; Khashoggi assessment) makes 'serious' the argued level for a state branding vehicle.

Majority-owned (60%) by Sela, a PIF company, with Turki Alalshikh as co-founder - Saudi state money at the core of the sport's newest major promotion. On top of the state record, the promotion is lobbying to weaken the Ali Act protections and tie fighter purses to its own rankings and belts.

Owned 100% by a serving Saudi government official (GEA chairman, royal-court adviser). The magazine runs the sport's most famous belt and rankings while its owner finances the cards its belts are contested on - the Guardian calls it 'the kingdom's own boxing magazine'. Concern rather than serious because it is a media/sanctioning brand, not a state fund vehicle.

US listed media company; no state stake or serious conduct record identified in the sources checked. The deal is notable (it funds the Saudi-majority venture to the reported tune of $100m a year) but the owner chain is clean.

These are brand relationships recorded as logos only - no contract terms or placements published.

Zuffa Boxing ownership split: 'Sela owns 60% of Zuffa Boxing and TKO owns 40%' - single source, Thomas Hauser, The Guardian, 28 Jan 2026 (https://www.theguardian.com/sport/2026/jan/28/zuffa-boxing-contract-dana-white-reform, fetched via curl). TKO's own 5 Mar 2025 release discloses no split; TKO's tkogrp.com news pages (fetched) carry no ownership item. Check TKO Group Holdings SEC filings for the definitive split.

The Ring acquisition: Turki Alalshikh's own X post (11 Nov 2024) says he 'finalized a deal to acquire 100% of The Ring Magazine'; the reported ~$10m price comes from Boxing Social (26 Feb 2026) and HeavyweightBoxing.com (16 Nov 2024, https://www.heavyweightboxing.com/post/turki-alalshikh-acquires-the-ring-magazine-a-new-era-begins, fetched - a low-profile secondary source). Neither confirms Golden Boy/Oscar De La Hoya as the seller of the 2024 deal (Golden Boy had bought The Ring in 2007). The New York Times/Athletic special report by Jacob Whitehead, 28 Apr 2025 ('Turki Al-Sheikh and the two sides of boxing's new king'), is cited by Wikipedia for the acquisition but is paywalled and unfetched.

Riyadh Season 2026-27 boxing programme: Wikipedia's Riyadh Season page (fetched) lists Canelo-Mbilli (31 Oct 2026) under the 2026-27 season but its fight rows carry [citation needed] tags; the ESPN 23 Jul 2026 article is the sourced date/venue anchor. Earlier Riyadh Season cards (Beterbiev-Bivol 12 Oct 2024, Ramirez-Billam-Smith 16 Nov 2024, Usyk-Fury II 21 Dec 2024, Beterbiev-Bivol II 22 Feb 2025, Canelo-Scull 3 May 2025) are on Wikipedia uncited; the archived UFC.com release (11 Jun 2025) independently confirms Riyadh Season staged Usyk-Fury, Beterbiev-Bivol twice, Canelo-Scull, Crawford-Madrimov (Los Angeles) and Joshua-Dubois (Wembley).

Sela ownership: sela.sa (fetched) shows a PIF logo in its footer and credits Sela with delivering WWE events in Saudi Arabia, but states ownership nowhere in words; the TKO release (5 Mar 2025) is the primary wording 'A Public Investment Fund (PIF) company, Sela'.
